data.name: Akshay
data.gender_notes: Akshay is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Akshay is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘akshaya’, which means ‘never-ending’, ‘unending’, or ‘immortal’. In Hindu mythology, the god of immortality is named Akshaya, and the name is also associated with Lord Vishnu. Akshay signifies the eternal and infinite nature of the universe and the self. The name Akshay carries the meaning “Immortal, Inextinguishable” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Akshay usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal, inextinguishable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the eternal and infinite nature of the universe and the self.
data.etymology: Akshay belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Immortal, Inextinguishable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Akshay total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Akshaya Tritiya, a Hindu festival celebrated on the third day (Tritiya) of the Shukla Paksha (bright fortnight) in the Hindu calendar month of Vaishakha. Akshaya means 'never diminishing'. It is believed that anything bought or started on this day will bring good fortune and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Akshay Kumar, an Indian film actor, born on September 9, 1967. His birth name was Rajiv Hari Om Bhatia. He adopted the name Akshay Kumar, which means 'never-ending, eternal' or 'invincible', as a blend of his father's name 'Hari Om' and the Sanskrit word 'akshay'.
